title: fix(post): a trailing Go home entry merges with the end-of-program home
body:
## What changed
A Go home as the **last** entry was written twice: once as the entry, then again as the post's own end-of-program home before `M30` (found in the hands-on check of #469).

**Seam: each post's own script.** The posts differ, so an app-level drop would be wrong. Siemens' end-of-program home is `G53 Z0` only, Fanuc writes `G49` before a trip home under TCPM, and the lathe homes X then Z.
- **New PRELUDE helper:** `linesWritten()`, documented in `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md`.
- **In each script:** the trip home records `homedAt`, and `onClose()` writes its own home only if a line was written since. In every post the trip home covers at least what the end-of-program home does.
- **Covered:** Fanuc, Haas, Mazak, Siemens 840D and Fanuc Lathe. Heidenhain and Tormach already refuse a trip home by name.
- **Unchanged:** mid-program homes, Suppress and "Skip pauses and homes".
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/504-trailing-home.md`.

**Fanuc tail:**
```
before            after
G91 G28 Z0        G91 G28 Z0
G28 X0 Y0         G28 X0 Y0
G90               G90
G91 G28 Z0        M30
G28 X0 Y0
M30
```

## How tested
- **New tests (`program_entry`):**
  - `a_trailing_home_entry_merges_with_the_program_end_home` (Fanuc, Haas, Mazak, Siemens 840D): one home for a trailing Go home; suppressed and skipped homes match the plain program; a mid-program home still gives two.
  - `the_lathe_post_writes_a_trailing_home_once`.
  - Both failed before the fix.
- **Goldens updated:** `program_entry/fanuc_pause_home.nc` and the Haas golden; each lost the duplicate home.
- **Gate:** the 31 app suites covering the posts (program_entry, posting, conformance, after_op, golden_cl, per_op_files, and the fanuc, lathe, tormach, inverted, coolant and probe post suites) and all camcraft-post tests pass. Clippy is clean.

## Not exercised
A machine or simulator run. The change only removes a duplicate home at program end.

Changelog: A Go home as the last entry is written once: it merges with the post's end-of-program home (Fanuc, Haas, Mazak, Siemens 840D, Fanuc Lathe) (#504)

Fixes #504

title: fix(app): a typed Slot's caps no longer read as a gouge
body:
## What changed

A typed Slot whose cutter reaches its round caps was reported as a Gouge on every plunge and feed, so it never posted (#510). The cause was the region the verifier checks a Slot against, `operation::material::stadium`. It drew each cap as 16 chords **inscribed** in the true arc. A chord sits up to `h(1 - cos 5.625°)` inside the arc, and the slot generator's passes follow the true arc exactly, so the gouge check (`d(centre, boundary) >= r - GOUGE_TOL`) flagged a cutter that only touched the cap.

The caps are now the polygon **circumscribed** about the arc. Every chord is tangent to the arc, and the corners sit at `h / cos(phi/2)`. The chord count is set per slot (`cap_segments`) so a corner stands at most `CAP_SAG_BUDGET = 0.001 mm` outside the arc, with 16 to 2048 chords per cap. The first and last corner of each cap lie on the lines of the straight sides, so the sides stay exact. `GOUGE_TOL` is unchanged.

**Posted G-code: unchanged.** The generator is untouched. Only the gouge verdict changes, plus the drawn region outline, which moves by at most 1 µm.

## Readings (80×60×20 stock, EM-0600-4FL, a=(-15,0), b=(15,0), Top 20, Bottom 10, stepdown 5)

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| width 6 (centreline pass) | `Gouge` at moves 2, 3, 7, 8, 12, 13; post blocked | no warnings; posts |
| width 10 (rings at ±2) | `Gouge` on all 18 plunges/feeds; post blocked | no warnings; posts |
| cap-centre distance to boundary (r = 3) | 2.9855 (needs ≥ 2.99) | ≥ 3.0 (tangent) |
| path pushed +0.05 mm in X past the cap | (already convicted) | still convicted |

## Top-Z pass

The issue also reports that a Slot makes a feed pass at its Top before stepping down. The other 2D ladders do the same: `cut_levels(top, bottom, step)` starts at Top for pocket, contour, circular, trace, face and the 3D entries. It is an air pass, never a gouge. This PR pins the current behaviour rather than changing one op on its own. The decision file explains why and recommends a separate issue if the first level should be `top - stepdown` for every ladder.

## Tests

New `crates/app/tests/slot_caps.rs`:
- `a_slot_riding_its_round_caps_verifies_clean_and_posts`: widths 6 and 10, each run with stock as the source and with a slotted part model as the source. Each run has no Gouge, no warning that blocks posting, and `post_setup` writes the program.
- `a_slot_driven_past_its_cap_is_still_a_gouge`: the generated path, shifted 0.05 mm past the cap and checked against the op's own `region_of`, is convicted. The unshifted path checks clean.
- `the_stadium_region_hugs_the_true_caps`: at 721 angles on both caps, the true arc is inside the region and a point 2 µm past it is outside.
- `the_slot_ladder_starts_at_the_authored_top`: the cut levels are [20, 15, 10].

Before the fix, the first three fail and the fourth passes.

Gate (debug): camcraft-app lib (101), slot_caps, operations, area_controls, cutting_data, project_roundtrip, golden_cl, verify and blind_floor all pass. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- The release `--ignored` lanes. No goldens move, because the generator output is unchanged.
- The UI region-outline drawing (the outline moves by at most 1 µm).
- Hand-run in the GUI or on a real machine.

Decision file: `docs/decisions/510-slot-cap-region.md`.

Changelog: A typed Slot whose cutter reaches its round ends is no longer falsely reported as a gouge, so it posts again (#510)

Fixes #510

title: fix(sim): judge spindle-C moves at the station pose and fixed steel in the machine frame
body:
Fixes a missed fixture hit under a spindle-C turn (#486). Two causes, both reproduced on main first.

## What was wrong
1. **Fixed steel was judged in the part frame only.** For a C move the live tool never leaves its station (+X), so steel there is hit at every C. The part-frame reading only saw it near C 0; `posed_steel::upright_turn` answers Unjudged for that pose, so the part-frame verdict stood. End to end: a Rotary Contour on the mill-turn C bar with a fixed steady at the station had no hit on the far side of the bar (C≈180), and the post gate was silent too.
2. **Steel riding the part was judged at the wrong pose.** `cl::stamp_c` gave every piece of a split move the move's end axis, while mid-turn the tool points along the diagonal. A chuck jaw on the diagonal at holder radius was silent.

## What changed
- `crates/cl/src/cl/rotary.rs`: `split` stamps each piece with the station pose at its own C (the move's axis turned by the turn left in the move). The last piece keeps the move's axis bit for bit. The post writes only C for C moves, so the stream and the `c_axis_helix.nc` golden are unchanged.
- New `crates/sim/src/verify/c_steel.rs`:
  - `station_poses` reads each C move's pose from its C, so toolpaths cached before this fix are judged right at the gate without regenerating.
  - `fixed_hits` judges fixed steel in the machine frame along the station ray.
  - The spindle line is recovered from the stamped tips, then from the op's rotary axis, and used only if every tip sits on its ray within 1e-4 mm. With no line, or an arc or non-finite C move, a C move against fixed steel is a hit (fails closed).
- `crates/sim/src/verify/workholding.rs`: both `_held` wrappers judge the station-posed path, then add the machine-frame fixed-steel hits. Add-only: no existing verdict loosens.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/486-stamp-c-axis.md`.

## How tested
- sim `c_axis_fixture` (8). Fail on main: `the_machine_meets_fixed_steel_at_the_station_mid_turn` (line given and line unknown), `a_rapid_turn_past_fixed_steel_convicts_as_a_rapid`, `steel_riding_the_part_meets_the_pose_the_turn_passes_through`, `every_stamped_piece_states_the_station_pose_at_its_own_c`. Also `a_path_stamped_before_486_is_read_at_the_pose_its_c_states`, plus clear and fail-closed controls.
- app `c_axis_fixture` (2): `fixed_steel_at_the_station_convicts_cuts_on_the_far_side_of_the_bar` (fails on main; checks generation and `posting::fixture_findings`) and an off-station control.
- Unit tests in `cl::rotary` and `verify::c_steel`.
- Quick gate (escalated to batch because `cl` changed): every suite green except the known headless-GPU ui tests (no adapter on this Mac). After merging main (#491's `arc_bulge`, a `mod` line conflict): sim `c_axis_fixture`, `posed_fixture`, `fixture_stack_span`, app `c_axis_fixture`, `fixtures` and `c_axis_live` pass; clippy `-D warnings` is clean on cl, sim and app.
- Verdicts in existing suites are unchanged; the only new verdicts are the newly caught hits.

## Not exercised
No posted G-code changes (C-only output and goldens unchanged), so no machine run is needed. May touch the same `verify/mod.rs` area as #488 (a `mod` line at most).

Changelog: Fixture checks under a spindle-C turn judge the tool at its machine station pose: fixed steel at the live-tool station and part-riding steel mid-turn are now caught instead of passing the post gate (#486)

Fixes #486

title: fix(sim): a chamfer or deburr owns its declared edge break
body:
## What changed

A 2D Chamfer or a Deburr generated with no warnings, but the post gate then refused it as a gouge. The program sim judged the bevel the op exists to cut against the model's sharp edge. This PR makes the op own its break, the issue's option 1. The bevel comes from the op's **stated** parameters, not from its moves.

- **`cl::EdgeBreak`** (new, `crates/cl/src/cl/edge_break.rs`): a record of the break the op was asked to cut. It holds the edge as a polyline at its own height, the bevel depth at the edge, and the slope. `floor_at(x, y)` gives the cone swept along the edge, limited to the stated plan width. It is carried on `cl::Toolpath::breaks` and is empty for every other kind.
- **Generators declare their breaks:**
  - `machining2d::chamfer` declares the picked loops at `top_z`, with depth `width*tan(angle)` and slope `tan(angle)`.
  - `finishing3d::deburr` declares its edge runs, with depth `drop` and slope `cot(half-angle)`.
  - Neither reads the declaration back off the moves.
- **Sim credit** (new, `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/edge_break.rs`, `credit_breaks`): this runs after `deviate`, from `simulate_document`. A gouge column inside a declared break's width, under a model top no higher than the edge, is re-judged against the bevel:
  - Cut down to the bevel (within `DEV_TOL`): clean.
  - Cut below the bevel: still a gouge, charged at its depth under the bevel.
  - Rest is untouched.
  - An edge nobody declared, or a boss standing above the edge, keeps the model's verdict.
  - `deviate` and `deviate_field` are not touched, so this stays clear of #481's `wall_slack.rs`.
- **Deburr skips steep edges** (generator fix, found while reproducing). The issue said the deburr's deeper gouge columns were link rapids. They were the vertical corner edges. A vertical cone riding a vertical edge, apex `drop` under each point, countersinks the corner down to the window floor. With the default window that is 9.8 mm on the 10 mm brick, a real gouge. The kernel now skips any edge that climbs steeper than the cone's flank, and says so in a path note.
- **Persistence:** the cached path gets an additive `breaks` key (`project/break_dto.rs`). Absent means none, so an old cache is judged against the sharp model until it regenerates (stricter, never looser).
- **Tilted (3+2) frames:** `TiltedFrame::world_path` translates the breaks when the frame is upright and drops them when it is tilted. A posed program is refused by the verdict anyway.
- **Multi-setup programs:** when the program spans setups that hold the part differently, only the final frame's ops' breaks are credited.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/303-op-owns-its-break.md`.

## Readings (upstream/main b2659dbe, brick 40x20x10, stock = brick, CM-0600-90)

| Job | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 2D Chamfer, kind defaults | `gouge: ... 624 cell(s), worst 0.74 mm` | gate clean, posts |
| Deburr, kind defaults (w 0.5, window = model) | `gouge: ... 495 cell(s), worst 9.80 mm at (19.94, -9.81, z 0.20)`: the vertical-corner countersink | gate clean, posts (4 vertical edges skipped, with a note) |
| Deburr, the issue's ride (w 2, tips z 6..8) | `gouge: ... 1544 cell(s), worst 3.80 mm` | gate clean, posts |
| Default chamfer, moves lowered 0.3 mm | - | `gouge: ... worst 0.30 mm` |
| Chamfer picks brick A, moves carried onto brick B | - | `gouge: ... worst 0.7x mm` |

## Tests

- `crates/app/tests/edge_break_gate.rs` (new, 5 tests):
  - `a_default_2d_chamfer_on_a_finished_brick_posts` (fails on main)
  - `a_default_deburr_on_a_finished_brick_posts` (fails on main)
  - `a_chamfer_ridden_deeper_than_its_stated_break_still_refuses`
  - `a_chamfer_on_an_edge_it_was_not_asked_to_break_still_refuses`
  - `the_declared_break_survives_save_and_load`
- `crates/sim/tests/edge_break_credit.rs` (new, 5 tests):
  - the declared chamfer is clean
  - over-deep is charged exactly 0.3
  - an undeclared edge keeps its full verdict
  - a boss above the edge is never credited
  - a sloped edge's bevel matches a brute-force swept cone
- `crates/motion/tests/chamfer_circular.rs`: `the_chamfer_declares_the_break_it_was_asked_to_cut` (new).
- `crates/app/tests/deburr_links.rs`: the #304 link test now rides a model with two blocks. The single brick, with its vertical edges skipped, is one run and has no link left to test.
- `crates/motion/tests/deburr.rs`:
  - `a_vertical_edge_is_skipped_out_loud_never_countersunk` (new).
  - `convex_creases_all_ride_a_closed_box_breaks_every_edge` renamed to `..._every_level_edge`. The box's level creases ride and its 4 vertical corners are skipped with a note.
  - `the_window_clips_along_the_edges_own_line` re-pinned on a sloped (1 in 2) rim, because the old curtain's vertical sides are now skipped.
- Test-literal updates for the new `Toolpath` field, with no behaviour change: sim rapids/pose tests, motion `one_descent`, app `turning_rapids_tests`.
- Gate results (debug):
  - `cargo test --no-fail-fast -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app`: 282 binaries, all green.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Release `--ignored` lanes:
  - all of `camcraft-sim`, plus app `operations`, `stock_sim_document` and `posting`: green.
  - app `stock_engine_agreement`: its 2 known-red tests (#494) fail as they do on main. That suite calls `deviate` directly, not `simulate_document`, so this change does not reach it.
- No golden changed. No chamfer or deburr goldens exist.

## Not exercised

- GUI Deviate view, by eye. A real cut.
- A chamfer on a 3+2 tilted frame: its breaks are dropped, and the posed verdict refuses it as before.
- Deburr edges that are shallower than the flank but whose adjacent face rises above the edge (a bottom rim ridden from above). The window keeps the default off them. If one is ridden, the sim still convicts it, correctly.

Changelog: A 2D Chamfer or Deburr on a finished part now posts: the program sim judges the op's declared edge break against its stated width and angle instead of the sharp model edge, while a deeper or undeclared break still refuses as a gouge; the deburr no longer rides vertical edges (it countersank the corners) and says so (#303)

Fixes #303

title: feat(post): probe positioning moves post as protected stop-on-contact moves
body:
## What changed

The positioning feeds of a probe cycle (the descent from the rapid / safe plane to each touch's start, the bore entry to its centre, the rise back to the safe plane) were plain G01. They now post as protected moves: stop on contact and alarm if the stylus trips on the way.

- **Stream:** `post::dump` marks every non-rapid straight move of a path that carries probing touches, other than the touches and their incremental back-offs, as a new `GUARD x y z F feed` record (`Record::Guard`, `probe_rec::GuardRec`, documented in `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md`). An arc or a feed with no rate in a probe path is refused with a WARN. The safe-plane rapids stay rapids.
- **Engine:** the new `onProbeGuard` hook (properties `X Y Z Feed`, `StartX/Y/Z`). A script without it is refused by name, once per operation. There is no PRELUDE default, because a plain feed would be the silent wrong answer.
- **Fanuc (`fanuc.cps`):** `G31 X.. Y.. Z.. F..`, then for each moving axis `IF[ABS[#506n-<end>]GT0.001]THEN#3000=3(PROBE HIT ON POSITIONING)`. This works because, with no skip signal, the skip position is the block end.
- **Tormach PathPilot (`tormach.cps`):** `G38.3 X.. Y.. Z.. F..`, then `oN if [#5070 EQ 1]` / `(MSG, PROBE HIT ON POSITIONING)` / `M2` / `oN endif`, with O-words from 5001.
- **Inverted axes (`invert.rs`):** a GUARD is mirrored like an absolute move.
- **Viewer map (`posting.rs`):** a GUARD counts as one motion record.

Sources (behaviour only): Fanuc's published custom macro B / G31 skip documentation (#5061-#5063, #3000); the LinuxCNC G-code reference (G38.3, #5070, O-code conditionals, MSG); Tormach's PathPilot machine-code reference (G38.2-G38.5 and M2 supported).

## Tests

- New `crates/app/tests/probe_guard.rs`:
  - `the_positioning_feeds_of_a_probe_path_are_marked_protected`: every mode; no plain feed left; GUARD count per mode; one record per move.
  - `the_guard_record_round_trips_and_refuses_malformed_lines`
  - `fanuc_writes_protected_moves_as_g31_with_a_contact_alarm`: new golden `nc/fanuc/probe_corner.nc`.
  - `tormach_writes_protected_moves_as_g38_3_with_a_trip_test`: new golden `nc/tormach/probe_guard_moves.nc`. It pins the guard blocks only, because Tormach's touches are #362 / PR #376.
  - `a_probing_post_without_on_probe_guard_is_refused_by_name`
- Regenerated Fanuc goldens: `probe_bore_centre`, `probe_corner_negative`, `probe_edge_negative_x`. The only change is G01 → G31 + the alarm line.
- `probe_op::the_posted_g31_z_is_the_tip_at_the_expected_contact` now tells touches from guards.
- Gate: these camcraft-app binaries are green, all run on the final head: conformance, fanuc_post, inverted_axis_display, inverted_equivalence, inverted_post, per_op_files, post_not_judged, posting, probe_guard, probe_op, probe_pick, probe_reach, project_roundtrip, scripting, tormach_machines, tormach_post. All camcraft-post tests are green. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- No real controller or PathPilot Hub run. The G38.3 / #5070 block and the Fanuc G31 alarm are checked against the documentation only.
- Tormach probe-op end to end: Tormach has no `onProbeMove` on main, so this waits for #376.

## Overlaps

- **#376 (Tormach G38.2):** my Tormach hook sits in its own section, away from #376's hunks. Its probe goldens will gain the G38.3 blocks.
- **#360 (Haas / Mazak / Siemens):** those scripts need `onProbeGuard`, or their probe ops are refused by name once this merges.
- **#465 (inverted probing):** `invert.rs` gets a separate Guard arm that mirrors without refusing, so it is covered by #465's translation.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/174-probe-protected-descent.md`.

Changelog: Probe op positioning moves (descent, bore entry, rise) post as protected stop-on-contact moves that alarm on an unexpected trip: G31 + #3000 on Fanuc, G38.3 + #5070 on Tormach PathPilot; a probing post without `onProbeGuard` is refused by name.

Fixes #174

title: test(sim): pin that the fixture box laws already convict every mesh penetration
body:
**Stacked on #476** (#339 slice 1, fixture mesh). Slice 2 of #339, answered by tests rather than new law. The full analysis is posted on #339.

## What this is
Slice 2 asked whether the mesh law must also **convict**: catch penetrations the box laws let through.

**Answer: no.**
- A meshed fixture's box is the exact AABB of the same transformed vertices the mesh law reads (`model::entity_world_aabb` / `world_facets`). `mesh_refined` only reads a mesh whose AABB equals the law's box, and non-finite meshes keep the box verdict. So the mesh always sits inside its box, rotated fixtures and overhangs included.
- Every deliberate silence of the box laws allows an overlap of at most `FIXTURE_HIT_TOL` (1e-9) with the box. That covers the strict z overlap in `band_hits_box` (c2, plus #464's d2 upper bands and flute column) and the strict-dip rule in `rapid_hits_box`. An overlap that small with the box can't be more than that with the mesh.
- Everything else is an enclosure, not a silence.

## What changed
New `crates/sim/tests/fixture_mesh_convict.rs` (5 tests, with a gate-map header). Each composes the box laws with `mesh_refined` the way `posting::fixture_problems` does.
- **A mesh top face keeps the strict dip:** a retract off it, a traverse riding it and a cut riding it are silent. The same moves 0.001 lower report Rapid and Flute.
- **A rotated fixture's top edge is its box's top:** a block turned 45° about X, then 30° about Z.
- **An overhanging arm convicts the stack under it:** the Shank under the arm and the Holder rim off its end both hit. Its top stays flush-silent.
- **The #424 and #425 repros convict on a closed mesh** (Holder), from the box law and the mesh alike.
- **No straight move the box laws clear penetrates the mesh:** a seeded sweep of 12,000 moves biased onto flush planes. 7,045 are silent (103 in flush contact), and none penetrates the mesh. Lowering the box top 0.01 mm makes this test fail at once, which shows it catches real gaps.

## Found along the way (filed separately)
**#491:** the box laws judge an XY arc by its **inscribed** chords at the bare band radius, so steel within the arc's sagitta (about 0.01 mm on R30) is missed. This applies to every fixture, not only meshed ones, so the fix belongs in the box law. It is out of this slice's scope.

## How tested
- `fixture_mesh_convict` 5/5, `fixture_mesh` 9 passed (1 ignored), `fixture_stack_span` 8/8.
- `clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.
- Test-only: no product code changes.

title: feat(ui): fixture UX - mark/import from the browser, mesh state, struck tint
body:
**Stacked on #476** (#339 slice 1, fixture mesh). Slice 4 of #339 per the triage on the issue: fixture UX.

## What changed
1. **Browser.**
   - A model row's context menu (under Models or a setup's Fixtures) offers **Use as fixture (<active setup>)** and **Stop using as fixture**. They reuse the existing `TagFixture` / `UntagFixture` commands, so undo and redo work.
   - A setup's Fixtures node offers **Import fixture…**, which reuses the existing dialog and activates that setup.
2. **Mesh state per fixture.**
   - Each Fixtures row ends in `mesh`, or `box only: <reason>`: open mesh, non-finite, collapsed, over the facet cap, no facets, or shared box. The reasons come from #476's `FixtureMesh::build`.
   - A mesh refusal is reported ahead of a shared box, since the user can fix it.
   - The Fixtures page shows the full sentence as a `Collision:` label.
   - The app helper is `fixture_view::mesh_states`, cached per document version.
3. **Highlight.** `FixtureHit` names the op, move and band, but not the fixture.
   - For the selected op, `fixture_struck::struck_by` re-runs the gate's own law against each fixture alone and keeps the ones that reproduce a warned move.
   - Those fixtures are tinted in the gouge colour, and the op banner names them ("Strikes fixture: …").
   - A warned move no fixture reproduces (e.g. a jaw moved without regenerating) says "Fixture not resolved for move N … regenerate to re-check" and tints nothing, rather than guessing.
   - Display only, cached per document version, op and path.

**Behaviour changes to note:**
- **Import as fixture is now one undo unit.** The new `ImportFixture` command applies and inverts the import, or the update of an existing name, together with the fixture marker. `crates/ui/tests/fixtures.rs::import_as_fixture_lands_as_two_undo_units` became `…_one_undo_unit`; the test count is unchanged.
- **A refused import now clears the pending fixture binding**, so it can't tag the next, unrelated import.
- **`posting::fixture_problems`'s per-op workholding check now calls `fixture_struck::op_hits`**, the same function the highlight uses, so the gate and the viewport can't disagree. Same logic, and app suites green.

`docs/decisions/339-fixture-ux.md`

## How tested
- App `fixture_ux` (8 tests):
  - closed, open and NaN mesh states, the shared box, and the version cache;
  - mark and unmark with undo;
  - `ImportFixture` fresh and as an update, with undo, redo and refusals;
  - the struck jaw is named and the clear one isn't;
  - a moved jaw is reported unresolved, not guessed;
  - no warnings resolves to nothing.
- UI `egui_app::fixture_ux_tests` (6 tests):
  - the menu rows and their commands, through the queue and undo;
  - the row suffixes;
  - the tint flag (exactly one part carries `STRUCK_CLASS`) and the banner line;
  - the unresolved banner;
  - the Fixtures page's refusal text.
- **No snapshot PNG touched.**
- App suites green. In ui, only the three headless-GPU tests fail (no adapter on this Mac), as on main. `clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --tests -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised (draft until the contributor's GUI check)
A hands-on check. A test kit is prepared: a project with a struck jaw, a clear jaw, an open-mesh jaw, and a plain model to mark.
